# APA Journal Article Reporting Standards

## Localization result

APA Journal Article Reporting Standards provide structured reporting expectations for quantitative, qualitative, and mixed-methods research so readers can evaluate design, analysis, and evidence.

## Core knowledge

- Quantitative reporting covers participants, sampling, design, measures, procedures, data diagnostics, analysis, estimates, uncertainty, effect sizes, and limitations.
- Qualitative reporting covers approach, research paradigm, researcher characteristics/reflexivity, context, recruitment, data collection, analysis, credibility, and findings.
- Mixed-methods reporting must explain the purpose and design of integration, timing, priority, procedures, and integrated inferences.
- Reporting standards are a completeness checklist, not a substitute for methodological quality.
- Use the standard at proposal time so required information and evidence are collected, not reconstructed later.

## Agent workflow

1. Select the correct JARS family and article/design subtype.
2. Convert checklist items into proposal fields and data-management requirements.
3. Audit the draft against the current standard before submission.

## Limits and stop conditions

- Journal-specific instructions may add or override presentation requirements.
- Standards can be updated; check capture date before final submission.
- Do not claim compliance when required information is unavailable.
